premises: Dislocation mobility in FeNiCrMn is controlled by a temperature- and strain-rate-dependent transition from thermally activated glide to drag.
Atomic-scale chemical inhomogeneity in solidified FeNiCrMn creates a spread in local activation energies for dislocation motion.
At low temperatures or high strain rates, reduced thermal assistance leads to dislocation drag and stress localization, increasing strength but reducing ductility.
At higher temperatures and lower strain rates, dislocations overcome barriers via thermal activation, maintaining ductility.
The dynamic response of FeNiCrMn can be explained solely by this dislocation mobility transition, without invoking other mechanisms like twinning or phase transformation.
